items.summary: Gilphas Eldragon, the founding patriarch of the Eldragon family, dedicated his entire life to the pursuit of absolute strength. In search of eternal combat, he consumed a legendary fruit rumored to grant immortality under the protection of the divine dragon. Yet the rumor was false—Gilphas aged, and in the end, passed away in his son’s arms. Or so it seemed. When he next opened his eyes, Gilphas found himself reborn a thousand years later as Zeke Eldragon, heir to his own bloodline. But the world had changed: the Eldragon clan now thrived under a ruthless creed of survival of the fittest, and a new threat known as the “Chaos” loomed over humanity. Faced with an unfamiliar era and even greater enemies, the ancient warrior feels only exhilaration. For Gilphas—now Zeke—this is the chance he longed for: “This time, I will witness the true end of martial strength!”

Ah, maintaining a character persona is truly hard.

items.title: The Misfit of the Martial World
items.time_updated: อัปเดตเมื่อ 1   d a y ,   1 9   h o u r s
items.summary: Tamlang, a Joseon warrior once notorious for his insolent arrogance, served as the Emperor’s personal bodyguard within the Chinese Imperial Palace. At the very center of power—a viper's nest of palace intrigue and assassination plots—he ruthlessly eradicated traitors at the root, earning a reputation as the Emperor’s sharpest blade. Yet, he refused to remain caged in a court where he never truly belonged. The Emperor hoped he would return to Joseon, but the news that eventually arrived was stunning: the realm's strongest combatant had abandoned absolute power to become a humble escort warrior at a small agency in the borderlands. Even the Emperor was left speechless by such an eccentric choice. The place Tamlang chose was the Ewha Escort Agency. On the surface, it is just an ordinary, mid-sized escort outfit, but Tamlang’s presence transforms their missions into something else entirely. Simply transporting goods becomes a perilous journey across warring factions and political power struggles, where a minor commission can ignite tensions across the entire martial world. It all begins with the marriage crisis of Peng Yerin, daughter of the Hebei Peng Clan. Refusing an arranged political marriage meant to preserve her clan's face, Yerin resolves to meet the Emperor herself and hires Tamlang as her personal bodyguard. Speeding through treacherous mountain paths to evade relentless pursuers, the two share a brief yet intense journey. Though Tamlang maintains his cold, stoic demeanor, the experience leaves an indelible mark on his life. It is a decisive moment of defending an individual's free will over cold political calculation. The subsequent Namgung Clan episode further skyrockets the Ewha Escort Agency's prestige. When Tamlang unleashes his Joseon martial arts in the clan's arena, he shatters the rigid pride of the prestigious family. Meanwhile, the arrival of the Sword Youth—who instantly reads the surging energy of the Ascending Dragon—hints at a massive shift in the Murim's power dynamic. Rather than conforming to the strict hierarchy of the Great Clans, Tamlang establishes himself as a force capable of shaking their very foundations. Around that time, the Zhurong Blade—a relic of pure legend—gains physical coordinates in reality. When the ancient poem of Chuiha Zhurong Peak is deciphered and three cups of liquor are poured at the Tanghyung Waterfall in Bosan, the rushing waters halt, unveiling the lost treasure of the Southern Kingdom. This discovery convulses the martial world. The Jeomchang, Hyeongsan, and Yunnan sects swarm in demanding a cut, turning negotiations into bloodbaths. However, Tamlang chooses mediation over massacre. He displays overwhelming force without overturning the board, elevating the Ewha Escort Agency into the linchpin of the Murim's balance of power. The Southern Kingdom’s treasure is no simple trove of gold; it is a war chest capable of funding armies and the key to overturning the Imperial succession. Amidst the escalating war for the throne, Princess Yeonhwa, the Emperor’s daughter, visits the Ewha Escort Agency. Outwardly a surveillance mission, her true objective is to gauge the dangerous variable known as Tamlang. Recalling his past intervention when the Emperor attempted to force her into a political harem, she approaches him with a volatile mix of political calculation and lingering personal emotion. Yet Tamlang never crosses the line. That unwavering emotional distance only heightens the razor-sharp tension between them. Simultaneously, a shadowy organization known as the Blood Flower makes its move. Marked by black robes, crimson flower crests, and the distinct curvature of Western crescent blades, their dark influence spreads. Even after the Three Blood Flowers are struck down, their mastermind refuses to step into the light. They monitor the Ak Clan, make clandestine contact with the King of Jenam, and the shadow of an entity called "The Master" looms ever darker. Whether the Blood Flower’s true target is the Southern Kingdom's treasure, the Imperial throne, or the unpredictable variable named Tamlang remains a deadly mystery. Ultimately, the missions of the Ewha Escort Agency become the transport of power and balance itself. Tamlang belongs fully to no faction, yet at the most critical junctures, he steps in to set the board right. A man who rejected being the Emperor’s blade to become an escort warrior on his own terms. He left the center of power, yet ultimately holds the scales of the entire realm in his hands. Belonging neither to the righteous Orthodox sects nor the ruthless Unorthodox factions, he refuses to conform to any established mold—a true **Misfit of the Martial World**.

items.summary: There was a hallmark of an ancient race, expelling the ghosts with exorcism; there came twelve people in a formation, who performed the exorcism by dancing. Bai Ze was a person who not only had knowledge of astronomy and geography but he also knew about trivialities. He could see through the past and understand the future. It was said that once he was asked by the Emperor to make the ‘Bai Ze Map of the Spirits and Monsters’, which consisted of 1,520 kinds of spirits and monsters. There was a book titled “Interrogation” in the pre-Qin dynasty. It taught the nations how to expel strange forces and spirits. There was a sage saying, “Respect the ghosts and demons but keep a distance from them. Don’t talk about strange forces and evil spirits.” The initial Heavenly Master named Zhang Daoling got from heaven the sword of female and male dragons and tigers. Getting rid of the heretical ritual performance, he cut down the assessment of the strange forces and evil spirits. Until the Ming dynasty, while Prince Zhu Biao inherited the throne, his younger brother Zhu Di served the country faithfully and took the responsibility of guarding the border of the country. He was granted the title: the great general. With one mind, the two siblings united and lived peacefully. There was an emperor of the Ming generation who loved the people so much that he resolved to guard the country until he breathed his last. Since the country was well guarded, the throne in that dynasty was able to be maintained by the next generations and could standstill for the next 500 years. Later, the rapid completion of modernization and evolution changed the name of Ming to China, and the domain was standing in the East. In 1,900 years of the Gregorian calendar, a meteor fell and covered eighty percent of the land area of the Blue Star. Thenceforward, the power of the supernatural revives; spirits and ghosts begin to awaken.
